title: States Newsroom: 19 of 22 ICE Shootings Began as Traffic Stops; DHS Accounts Repeatedly Disputed
excerpt: A States Newsroom review found that 19 of the 22 people shot by federal immigration officers during Trump's second term were fired upon during vehicle stops, and that independent video had contradicted the DHS account in multiple cases.
content:
Following the fatal shooting of Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Maine on July 13, 2026 — the 22nd person shot by federal immigration officers during Trump's second term — States Newsroom published a comprehensive review of all shooting incidents.

The review found that 19 of 22 shooting incidents involved DHS officers firing upon people in their vehicles during traffic stops. In at least five cases, DHS brought charges against those shot, accusing them of being the aggressors, only for those charges to be subsequently dismissed. ICE's rapid initial public statements have repeatedly failed to hold up under scrutiny from independent video or witness testimony.

  • The 22 shooting incidents spanned the country, from Colorado to Texas to Oregon to New Jersey.
  • In the moments after each shooting, DHS consistently accused those fired upon of using their vehicles as weapons against officers.
  • Former acting ICE director John Sandweg told CNN that officers 'aren't being as patient' as they would normally be due to mounting White House pressure to ramp up arrests, causing them to attempt stops while targets are still in motion.
  • Neither Salgado Araujo nor Durán Guerrero were the intended targets of their respective enforcement operations, DHS officials confirmed.
